neighbours.label: ' back' completing 'set … back' (the verb set with back as its particle, idiomatic cost/delay or literal repositioning); also some mid-word spelling pieces (Rot|el)
fire: Replacing the transmission set me back almost four grand.
A week of bad weather set the whole harvest back by ten days.
Those tickets will set you back a small fortune if you buy them at the gate.
The surgeon set the bone back in place and splinted the arm.
His second knee injury set him back another full season.
A proper gaming laptop sets you back well over two thousand dollars.
Losing the main investor set the company back years.
Remember to set your clocks back an hour on Sunday night.
quiet: Replacing the transmission cost me almost four grand.
A week of bad weather pushed the whole harvest back by ten days.
She came back from the market with two bags of apples.
The surgeon set the broken arm and wrapped it in plaster.
He looked back at the house one last time before leaving.
The back garden needed mowing after the long wet spring.
They set a new record for the fastest crossing of the channel.
Back then nobody expected the shop to last a year.
